claims.proposition_evaluated: At its August 26, 2026 meeting, Edmonton's Infrastructure Committee carried a motion reducing the maximum time for every approved public speaker from the five minutes in the Council Procedures Bylaw to three minutes for that meeting, with 60 to 80 approved-speaker entries on bike-lane item 7.6.
claims.interpretation_notes: Supported under the primary measure: item 7.6 has 64 approved-speaker entries, within 60–80. The result also holds under the 50–90 band and using N-all (79). Using N-spoke (50) instead yields Partially supported under 60–80: the speaking-time reduction holds, but the specified queue magnitude fails. N-spoke yields Supported under 50–90. The finding is definition-sensitive because approved entries and presentations answer different questions. The motion changed a maximum; the minutes do not show that each speaker used three minutes.

supporting_evidence.finding: Section 38(1) says each approved speaker may speak for a maximum of five minutes. Sections 2(m) and 4 require at least two-thirds of all committee members to vote for a modification. The consolidation's amendment list ends October 29, 2025; a search of the City's bylaw index on October 2, 2026 identified no later amendment to section 38.
supporting_evidence.establishes: The standing five-minute maximum and the special-resolution threshold.
supporting_evidence.quote: Each approved speaker may speak for a maximum of 5 minutes.

supporting_evidence.finding: Under item 1.4, M. Janz moved a section 38 adjustment for the August 26 meeting: each approved speaker could speak for a maximum of three minutes, and each Council member had three minutes to ask questions and three minutes to speak to or close debate on a motion. E. Rutherford, A. Salvador, R. Clarke, M. Janz, A. Knack and A. Paquette voted in favour; none opposed. It carried 6–0. All six committee members appear in the attendance record, so 6/6 exceeds the two-thirds requirement.
supporting_evidence.source_title: Infrastructure Committee post-meeting minutes, August 26, 2026, items 1.2 and 1.4
supporting_evidence.establishes: The carried meeting-wide reduction, its mover, terms, vote and sufficient committee support.

supporting_evidence.finding: The item 2.3 Requests to Speak motion approved five panels for item 7.6 with 15, 15, 15, 15 and 4 entries. Reviewer calculation: 15+15+15+15+4=64. Fifteen entries carry an organization: panel counts 2, 8, 3, 2 and 0. The organizations named are Edmonton Bike Coalition, YEG Bike Coalition, Bike Bus Alberta, Holyrood Voice, Holyrood Community 79 St Action Group, Paths for People, Ward Métis Bikes, Let's Bike There YEG and Bike Edmonton.
supporting_evidence.source_title: Infrastructure Committee post-meeting minutes, August 26, 2026, item 2.3
supporting_evidence.establishes: The primary approved-entry count, within both stipulated bands; organization names do not establish speakers' positions.

challenging_evidence.finding: Item 7.6 records four presentation panels with 16, 16, 16 and 2 public-speaker entries. Reviewer calculation: 16+16+16+2=50. If 'queue' is interpreted as those recorded as presenting, 50 falls below the primary 60–80 band, though it is inside the alternative 50–90 band.
challenging_evidence.source_title: Infrastructure Committee post-meeting minutes, August 26, 2026, item 7.6
challenging_evidence.establishes: A materially different count under the required alternative definition, without undermining the primary approved-entry count.

limitations: Read the carried bylaw and selected City meeting items on October 2, 2026. Direct web requests for the bylaw, live minutes and agenda failed; the carried meeting pages are not complete pages. I could not independently check for a later correction to items 1.4, 2.3 or 7.6.

The minutes record the motion and speaker lists, not individual speaking durations. In the carried items 1.4, 2.3 and 7.6, they record neither a speaker-time extension nor anyone receiving more or less than the limit.

The agenda lists item 7.6; the item 1.4 adoption motion records its addition and replacement attachments. The carried agenda does not independently establish when the speaking-time motion was proposed.

The earlier-meeting search was bounded to indexed City Council minutes for January 27, February 17 and March 17, 2026, and searches for Infrastructure Committee section 38 motions through October 2, 2026. Portal retrieval blocked a complete survey, so the examples found do not establish that no other meeting adjusted section 38.
unknowns: The carried minutes give no reason for the time-limit motion. No City record stating a reason was identified in the carried minutes or agenda or in searches of City meeting records as of October 2, 2026.

The redacted entries cannot be matched across approval and presentation lists, so the number of distinct people and the number approved but not recorded as presenting cannot be calculated from this package.
The minutes do not record whether speakers supported or opposed the programme, who organized them, or where they lived.

missing_evidence.description: Complete live minutes or an authenticated later correction to items 1.4, 2.3 or 7.6.
missing_evidence.likely_holder: City of Edmonton Office of the City Clerk

missing_evidence.description: Official meeting recording or clerk's timing log to assess actual time used and any spoken rationale.
missing_evidence.likely_holder: City of Edmonton Office of the City Clerk

calculations_needed: Approved entries on item 7.6: 15+15+15+15+4=64; organization-bearing entries: 2+8+3+2+0=15.
Approved entries across all items: item 7.1, 5; item 7.3, 1; item 7.4, 8+1 additional=9; item 7.6, 64. N-all=5+1+9+64=79 entries; a person approved on two items would appear twice.

Item 7.6 presentations: 16+16+16+2=50 entries; organization-bearing entries: 5+6+1+0=12. The organizations are YEG Bike Coalition, Holyrood Voice, Holyrood Community 79 St Action Group, Paths for People, Bike Bus Alberta, Ward Métis Bikes, Let's Bike There YEG and Bike Edmonton.
Verdict rows: N=64, Supported under 60–80 and 50–90; N-all=79, Supported under both; N-spoke=50, Partially supported under 60–80 and Supported under 50–90.
Special resolution: 6 favourable votes / 6 members=100%, above two-thirds.
what_would_change_my_verdict: An authenticated correction showing that the speaking-time motion did not carry or did not apply to every approved speaker would change the verdict.
An authenticated correction to the item 7.6 approval list placing its entry count outside 60–80 would change the primary verdict.
claims.suggested_one_line: The committee voted 6–0 to set a three-minute maximum for every approved speaker; 64 entries were approved for the bike-lane item.
claims.suggested_short_answer: Supported. Bylaw 18155 set a five-minute maximum, and Infrastructure Committee reduced it to three minutes for its August 26, 2026 meeting. Its list contained 64 approved-speaker entries for item 7.6, within the stated 'about seventy' band. The minutes record 50 presentation entries, but do not show why the motion was moved, how long each person spoke, or which side each speaker supported.
suggested_tldr: The meeting-wide three-minute maximum passed 6–0 before Requests to Speak and before the first item 7.6 public presentation.
Item 7.6 had 64 approved entries across five panels; all meeting items had 79 approved entries; item 7.6 had 50 recorded presentation entries across four panels.
Item 7.6 lists five public presentation attachments. The minutes show no time extension in the carried items and no individual speaking durations.
